'''''Solanum linnaeanum''''' is a [[Solanum|nightshade]] [[species]] known as '''devil's apple''' and, in some places where it is introduced, '''apple of Sodom'''. [[Apple of Sodom (disambiguation)|The latter name]] is also used for other nightshades and entirely different plants elsewhere, in particular the poisonous [[Asclepiadoideae|milkweed]] ''[[Calotropis procera]]''.<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | ''Calotropis procera'' | 8653 | accessdate = 3 September 2014}}</ref>

This [[poisonous plant]] bearing [[tomato]]-like fruit is native to many African countries [[Kenya]], [[Tanzania]], [[South Africa]],<ref>AWC (2004)</ref> Zimbabwe and Mozambique,<ref name="ReferenceA">Species Fact Sheet, Queensland Government</ref> and is considered to be an [[invasive species in Australia]],<ref>DAF-WA [2006]</ref> [[New Zealand]],<ref>Roy ''et al.'' (2005)</ref> [[Hawaii]], [[Fiji]], [[New Caledonia]], other [[Pacific Islands]], the Aseer region of Saudi Arabia, and northern areas of Pakistan.<ref>[http://www.hear.org/pier/species/solanum_linnaeanum.htm Information on Solanum linnaeanum as relevant to Pacific Islands] also in Aseer region in Saudi Arabi and northern areas of Pakistan</ref> When raw its fruits are green and look exactly like the Thai eggplant and when ripe they are yellow. In Ukambani eastern Kenya children in the villages in summer season use the poisonous yellow fruit as football, cautiously.

Solbec Pharmaceuticals attempted to [[drug development|develop]] [[Coramsine]],<ref>SP [2006]</ref> a 1:1 mixture of the [[alkaloids]] [[solamargine]] and [[solasonine]] extracted from ''Solanum linnaeanum'', as a cancer drug. Preliminary clinical trials were initially promising,<ref>Millward ''et al.'' (2005)</ref> but the drug was ultimately unsuccessful.

''Solanum linnaeanum'' may be confused with ''[[Solanum cinereum]]'' (Narrawa burr) in Australia,<ref name="ReferenceA"/> the neotropical ''[[Solanum capsicoides]]'',<ref name="ReferenceA"/> or ''[[Solanum incanum]]'' in Africa.

==Synonyms==
Due to confusion about what species the original ''Solanum sodomeum'' of [[Carl Linnaeus]] referred to (most recently, it was identified as ''[[Solanum ferox]]''), the old description was discarded and the plant redescribed as currently understood. A new [[taxon]] honoring Linnaeus was chosen. A number of invalid taxa have thus become attached to the devil's apple:<ref name = ss2008>Solanaceae Source (2008)</ref>
* ''Solanum astrophorum'' <small>Jan (''[[nomen nudum]]'')</small>
* ''Solanum hermannii'' <small>Dunal</small>
* ''Solanum mccannii'' <small>Santapau</small>
* ''Solanum sodomeum'' <small>L.</small> (disputed)
* ''Solanum sodomeum var. hermannii'' <small>(Dunal) Dunal</small>
* ''Solanum sodomeum var. mediterraneum'' <small>Dunal</small>
* ''Solanum undatum'' <small>Bouton ex Dunal ([[Solanum undatum|preoccupied]])</small>
:''Solanum undatum'' as described by Walsh is ''[[Solanum lycocarpum]]''.
:''Solanum undatum'' var. ''violaceum'', described by Dunal in [[A. P. de Candolle|de Candolle]], is the original ''[[Solanum aethiopicum]]'' of Linnaeus.

It is not clear whether the plant described by [[Johann Franz Drège|Drège]] as ''Solanum sodomeum'' was of this species. ''Solanum sodomeum'' by Russ based on [[Christian Gottfried Daniel Nees von Esenbeck|Nees von Esenbeck]] is another ''nomen nudum''.<ref name = ss2008 />
